free_tier.stated: 1 GiB PER FILE in the project *file release* area - a separate, much smaller surface than the PPA. The manual says: 'Each individual file must be no more than 1 GiB and you must be the: project maintainer / project driver / or the series release manager.' There is no published total-per-project cap; the unit of accounting is the individual release file. (The 8 GiB figure widely quoted for Launchpad is the PPA disk quota, verified in round 2 - it does not govern file releases.)

egress.terms: Free, no billing. Files are served from launchpadlibrarian.net behind a 303 redirect. No published transfer cap; round 2 measured ~70 KB/s single-stream on a PPA .deb, which is a throughput problem rather than a quota one.

tooling: Web upload per release ('Add download file') is the documented path - no SFTP/rsync equivalent to Savannah or SourceForge for the release area. Automation goes through the Launchpad web service API: `launchpadlib` (Python), the `+download` URL shape, and hardware-bound API tokens. Consumer side is plain HTTPS GET with an MD5 and optional GPG signature per file.
chaining: unlimited projects x unlimited series x unlimited releases x 1 GiB per file. At 1 GiB granularity 500 GB is 500 files - feasible but operationally noisy, and every upload is a web action unless scripted via launchpadlib. Distinct from the PPA path (8 GiB/PPA, .deb-only, dput/rsync upload).
limits_note: per-object-cap: 1 GiB hard per release file. Also content-typed: files must fall into 'code release tarball / installer files / README or other documentation / changelog file / release notes' - arbitrary blobs are off-spec. retention: indefinite per release. request-rate: not documented for the file area; the docs page itself is flagged 'migrated from help.launchpad.net as is, and has not yet been revised'.
